query: After the token embeddings are projected in ColBERT, how are they normalized, and what equivalence and value range does this give to their dot products?

drafts: ColBERT 对投影后的 token 嵌入进行归一化，使每个嵌入的 L2 范数等于 1 [1][2]。由此，任意两个嵌入的点积等价于其余弦相似度，取值范围为 [−1, 1] [1]。

requirements.reason: 问题要求说明ColBERT投影后token嵌入的归一化方式及其点积的等价关系和取值范围。回答涵盖全部三点：L2范数归一化为1、点积等价于余弦相似度、取值范围[-1,1]，主体与条件均正确。

citations.quote: Finally, the output embeddings are normalized so each has L2 norm equal to one. Te result is that the dot-product of any two embeddings becomes equivalent to their cosine similarity, falling in the [−1, 1] range.

cited_sources.text: Finally, the output embeddings are normalized so each has L2 norm equal to one. Te result is that the dot-product of any two embeddings becomes equivalent to their cosine similarity, falling in the [−1, 1] range.

In summary, given q = q0q1...ql and d = d0d1...dn, we compute the bags of embeddings Eq and Ed in the following manner, where # refers to the [mask] tokens: Eq := Normalize( CNN( BERT(“[Q]q0q1...ql##...#”) ) ) (1) Ed := Filter( Normalize( CNN( BERT(“[D]d0d1...dn”) ) ) ) (2) 3.3 Late Interaction Given the representation of a query q and a document d, the rel- evance score of d to q, denoted as Sq,d, is estimated via late in- teraction between their bags of contextualized embeddings.
